lines.text: Mind the gap by the west doors. We promised the fire officer four metres and he brought a tape.
R. MALLORY is written on the folder spine. The rota has gone soft where her thumb keeps the rain off.
Are you all staying until morning?
That is the idea. Some have the first bus to catch. The rest have work, which is why the cups are numbered.

choices.text: Ask what the rota is for.
Let her get back to the list.

lines.text: The gate notice still says fourteen days.
It has said fourteen days since March. The contractor sheet says first strike, 06:00 Thursday, 1967 wing.
I rang the number at the bottom. A man confirmed it, asked where I got the number, and hung up.
Why number the cups?
So I know who has gone home without making them announce it. At quarter past, I cross out anyone who misses the check.
Nothing dramatic happens. A coat disappears, a flask gets lighter, and the list tells me whether I should ring somebody.
Mostly they stand in the rain and say what it was like. One or two say he.
Not yet. Same rain, same names. Keep the service lane clear if you go round again.
You are back. Keep right of the banner; somebody has put a chair behind you.
Still six?
Still six. Vans through this lane at five forty, horn at five fifty-five. That is the last call I had.
If you leave before then, use the road gate. They will chain the service side first.

choices.text: Ask whether the work is still scheduled.

lines.text: Third window along, second floor. The black tape is mine. They charged me for taking it down.
LEILA is written around the flask lid in fading marker.
What was in there?
Practice room P-3. Marimba if you booked early, snare drum if you did not, and a click coming back through the partition.
How far behind was it?
Not enough to count cleanly. Enough to pull the stick out of your hand if you listened to it.
Maintenance packed the grille twice. After that I practised with one earplug and stopped booking evenings.

choices.text: Ask how late it came back.

lines.text: Why come back for the demolition?
Ruth emailed the old students. I deleted it, then found the timetable still saved on my phone.
I wanted to see whether the tape was there. It is. I have not worked out whether that helps.

choices.text: Ask why she kept the timetable.

lines.text: Still there. The tape catches the yard light when the rain changes.

choices.text: Ask why she kept the timetable.

lines.text: You were in there long enough for the light behind P-3 to go out twice.

choices.text: Tell her what the room did.

lines.text: The return is still there.
Then maintenance packed it twice for nothing. That is useful, even if it is not an answer.
Write down which room before you sleep. Morning moves things around.
She rubs the rain from the flask lid with her thumb.
The booking sheet called it P-3, even after the brass number came off.

choices.text: Describe it without naming a cause.

lines.who: THE MAN WITH THE OLD KEYS
lines.text: That lock was changed after I left. Same escutcheon, new barrel. They did not bother changing the paint around it.
An old label reads O. PRYCE / SOUTH PORCH. The ring no longer carries the key it names.
What happened to the porch key?
Returned with the rest. The diocese signed for twelve keys and sent me a receipt for eleven.
How many bells are up there now?
Six now. Eight before 1964. Two went for scrap and the inventory kept copying the old number.
The tenor is heavy for the frame. You feel the tower take the stroke before the note reaches the yard.
Why is there no handle outside?
The pull was removed during the alarm work and never put back. The fixing holes are still under the paint.
From the nave you can leave. From the forecourt you need somebody already inside. That passed inspection somehow.

choices.text: Ask why the west door cannot be entered.

lines.text: No change. New barrel, old rain running down it.
The tower moved while you were gone. Only a little. The water changed direction on the lead.
What did you ring the tenor for?
Deaths, mostly. One stroke for each year, then the tenor once more after the pause.
You listened from the street and counted. If you knew the family, the number was enough.
He lets the old key ring settle against his coat.
The pause mattered.

choices.text: Ask what the tenor was used for.

lines.text: Hold that corner, would you? The sleeve kept the rain out. The hole I punched in it did not.
The catalogue card beneath her hand reads OKAFOR, D. / LAUNDRY SITE.
Is that this park?
Laundry yard, 1912. Same boundary wall. The grass came in 1974 and the caption changed to municipal open space.

choices.text: Ask what is marked for salvage.

lines.text: What have you got from inside Ellery?
Baths opening, chapel dedication, four class photographs, a fire drill. Then the run stops in 1986.
After that I have two press photographs and the planning PDF. If somebody used the rooms, they kept the camera away.
What is marked for salvage?
The foundation stone. The mosaic is photograph only. Nothing lists the practice-room doors.
I asked for one hour inside with a camera. The answer arrived after the contractor fence did.

choices.text: Ask what the contractor will keep.

lines.text: The labels are drying now. Pick one before I put them away.

choices.text: Ask what is marked for salvage.

lines.text: You had equipment inside. Did you write the room names down, or only the take numbers?

choices.text: Tell her what the recorder kept.

lines.text: Room names, start times, and whatever came through the walls.
Good. Put the names on the case before you hand it over. Take numbers mean nothing once the sheet is separated.
Make two copies. One for the client, one somewhere the client does not tidy.
She turns the sleeve over and presses the damp corner against a folded bar towel.
Keep the case label with both.

choices.text: Say what is on the tape.

lines.text: Keep it out of the bar light. On the plastic, the pencil goes silver when it catches straight on.
M. VEY is printed beneath an old library stamp. Two chapel plans have been taped over the street map.
What are the two circles?
Ellery chapel and St Brendan’s crossing. Different plans, different scales. I copied the centres before the archive shut.
That runs through both chapels.
Centre to centre, within what I can do with photocopies. There is no duct or right of way on either plan.
It may be nothing. But if you stand in one of them tonight, listen for the other before the machinery arrives.
Why draw the line in the first place?
A neighbour said the drain covers answer the tenor. I tried the bearings and found this.
The neighbour may be wrong. My centres may be wrong. The line is still straighter than I expected.
And that is enough to stay here all night?
It is enough to keep the map dry until six.

choices.text: Ask where the idea came from.

lines.text: Same line. I checked after you left; the tape has not improved it.

choices.text: Ask where the idea came from.

lines.text: You came back by the long side of the line. From this stool I can see the door.
Give the map back.

choices.text: Ask what he expects at six.

lines.text: What happens to your line at six?
One centre disappears. After that nobody can repeat the measurement, including me.
If anything answers the first strike, everybody here will hear it. That is as far as I can take the claim.

choices.text: Ask what the first strike changes.

lines.text: Mind the cable. The black one is mine; the orange one belongs to somebody who left before dinner.
KIT is written on the recorder strip. Rain has lifted the K at one corner.
What are you taking off the wall?
Low end, mostly. Traffic, plant, wind loading. I am trying to leave enough headroom for the first machine.

choices.text: Ask what the microphone is aimed at.
Ask to see the gain log.
Ask what would make the take useful.

lines.text: What happened when the plant stopped?
Plant drops at twenty-two thirty. The floor loses eleven dB. One narrow band stays where it was.
Could be road loading, the river wall, or a pump on another supply. I do not have enough baselines.
Does it move?
About half a semitone in forty minutes, then back. Slow enough that temperature is still in the argument.
What would count as a clean result?
A before-and-after. Plant off, road quiet, rain noted, microphone unmoved. Then I can compare Thursday.
At the moment it is one wet night and a line on a screen. Interesting is not the same as identified.

choices.text: Ask what would make the recording useful.

lines.text: Cable is still live. Come round the back if you want the meter again.

choices.text: Ask what changed with the plant.
Ask what would make the take useful.

lines.text: You had the field side. Did your low cut stay in, or did you take it flat?
Flat. The floor moved under it, but the recorder stayed level.
Then note the suspension and the room before anything else. “Moved” will be the first word everybody argues with.
I can compare the times if you give me the slate later. Keep your original.

choices.text: Describe the movement without naming it.

lines.text: The rain has taken the ink at the edges. Six o’clock is still legible.
Every cup goes back to the same flask.
Nobody is watching the road.
The red tally light makes the shut porch look occupied.
The date has been corrected in three different hands.
They have left the machines a way in.
Through the windscreen: nine coats, one folded chair, the banner still tied to the railing.
The people at the gate make room. A chair opens; a dry coat appears from somewhere behind it.
His pencil line. Chapel to chapel. I had been standing at the other end.
That should have been dealt with. Properly. I do not see why the rest of us should lose the building over it.
Her thumb returns to the rota. The column after six is headed LESSONS / RESTART.
They asked for acknowledgment before rehearsal. Your sheet has them starting again.
It is a proposal. You have to give people something to come back to.
My daughter had a lesson here on Saturdays. We made a morning of it. I would like the next families to have that.
What if the students still do not want to play?
Then we ask what would make them feel able. We cannot keep every room shut indefinitely.
There it is: a timetable with room for everything except an answer that stays no. I can hear it in hers more easily than in my own.
What would you actually have happen if the machines turn back?
Lessons, the bells, people in and out. It is not much of a square with every door shut.
Of course somebody would have to make it safe first. I am not proposing we personally run the place.

Keep the instruction as well as the recovery entry. Otherwise somebody can call the missing label a clerical delay. / Keep the room name with the receipt. Do not let them file the bodies under a building nobody can point to. / An account to keep with the official entry. Not to replace it. The disagreement is part of what they did.
And a transfer receipt does not tell us why somebody died. Neither does a photograph.
Do you still want the rooms preserved after that?
I asked for an hour to photograph them. I did not ask the students to give another recital.
She aligns the sleeves. The empty room is something she can keep. An occupied one might refuse the photograph.
Bricks coming down will not amend the record. Keeping them up will not amend it either.
